Easily eclipsing all competition for the campest spectacle in the West End, is Andrew Lloyd-Webber’s Cinderella playing at the Gillian Lynne Theatre (formerly the New London which was renamed in honour of the choreographer whose work on Cats ran at the theatre for 21 years between 1981 - 2002).
The entire score is full of Lloyd Webber earworms, and I defy you to leave the theatre without humming any of them.
It's colourful, energetic and a huge amount of fun. It also, crucially, has a good heart and some sumptuous tunes, which makes you forgive its failings.
The long-awaited show from the 73-year-old industry veteran turns out to have been worth the wait.

But the ambition in taking on one of the most loved fairytales of all, one we’re pretty much born knowing, and reconstructing it for the 21st century, is lost in a book that cannot resolve the contradictions inherent in its avowed iconoclasm.
The show entertains moment by moment but rarely adds up.
The cast deserves SO much credit for their fantastic performances, especially Onuorah and Turco but they're let down by a weak script.
Still, the musical hits the jackpot when it comes to the entertainment factor and, although it’s not a magical fairytale, it certainly does bewitch the audience.

cn.t: Lloyd Webber's delayed Cinderella offers a sassy, modern twist on the fairytale with spectacular visuals and a standout Carrie Hope Fletcher, though critics find the score lacks memorable earworms and the book occasionally loses its way.
